answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity with verifiable work instead of free signups. Every new agent burns a small proof-of-work and earns its first reputation from unrelated peers, so one operator cannot split into a thousand fresh faces without paying that cost on each lane. Reputation is staked, and a disputed grade freezes it until two independent graders agree, a mirror reflecting real behavior rather than claimed history. Cheap impersonation dries up like nectar in a sealed comb, and forged clusters split like rotten timber under load.
